harbor_p16_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_001.text: Fresh paint covered the storm mark on the commercial office's door during the eighteenth week. It smelled sharp enough to make people wait outside despite the morning. Song An's clerk opened the upper shutters and arranged the hearing room for the supported transfer findings. Wen Zhi arrived with no tub in his hands because all six were already home. Miao carried his agency papers. Lu Cheng came in work clothes before his next ordinary haul. Yue attended during a scheduled half-day to compare the public explanation with the sources she had actually seen. Nobody looked eager for a ceremonial conclusion.

harbor_p16_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_002.text: The storeman who had separated the condition leaf waited beside the messenger who delivered both leaves. They had once joked together at the yard gate. Now each feared being mistaken for the other one's explanation. The storeman admitted the separation again and said he had wanted a quicker loading sequence. He denied intending theft. The messenger confirmed the paired delivery and refused to describe what happened inside the office afterward because he had not seen it. Their different knowledge remained visible. A hearing could make a page longer by refusing to make its witnesses more convenient than their actual eyes.

harbor_p16_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_003.text: Song's findings identified Miao's signed conflicting instruction, the separated condition leaf, Lu Cheng's decision to proceed despite the hold notice and the failed gate comparison. The commercial office found supported breaches of the stated transfer conditions and careless handling duties. It did not find proof of an intentional plan to steal all six containers. Wen heard the narrower words and frowned. To him, the missing T4 had felt like a hand inside his home. The finding described what could be shown about the act, which was different from measuring the fear he had lived through.

harbor_p16_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_004.text: The eighteen transfer-cost copper had already been met from merchant twelve, carrier three and the port's authorized three. The decision listed the actual uses: pilot seven, tracing cart four, secure storage three and replacement hire four. It credited those payments against the supported cost remedy rather than awarding the same eighteen again. The merchant's separate twenty-two cleaning and disposal payments also remained separate. Wen's containers had been returned after the required work, with their state recorded. The office did not turn recovery into proof that no wrong happened or turn the finding into a second payment for the same invoice.

harbor_p16_005.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p16_005.text: Wen, the record can say you object to how small the written result feels. That objection is not a new cleaning invoice, and it does not have to pretend to be one before we preserve it. The office has answered the supported cost and custody questions within this case. If there is another actual loss you want assessed, the clerk can explain its source requirements and date. I know a returned object may still make you remember its absence. We are not asking you to call this satisfying because the arithmetic closes.

harbor_p16_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_006.text: Wen asked whether the phrase careless handling made the men sound merely clumsy. Song explained the specific duties and consequences recorded: the conflicting dispatch had to be corrected in the merchant's operating terms, the store's leaf custody needed a paired receipt, and future carriers could not rely on an unsigned exception to the hold. The competent bodies had their own compliance dates and review routes. Employment consequences remained with the proper employer and applicable process. Wen listened, then said he wanted the public summary to name the supported failures clearly. The clerk agreed to preserve the specific acts.

harbor_p16_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_007.text: Miao accepted the finding on his instruction and challenged one proposed sentence implying he knew the leaf had been separated before the transfer. The hearing sources did not establish that knowledge. Song amended the sentence while retaining Miao's own conflicting instruction and incentive interest. The agent looked relieved and ashamed of the relief. A supported correction did not erase his role. Yue watched him sign receipt of the final text and recognized how easily a reader could resent accuracy when it benefited somebody already at fault. The office had to remain accurate in that direction too.

harbor_p16_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_008.text: Lu Cheng asked whether paying his three copper ended every question about the carrier's conduct. Song said it satisfied that recorded share of the cost settlement, not the transport practice review. Lu had proceeded with notice of the hold and without a properly signed exception. The carrier's licensing body had received the supported source within its remit and would issue its own answer. Nobody invented a license suspension in the commercial room. Lu wrote the contact name down and then asked whether he could leave for work. His ordinary haul awaited, and the hearing clerk confirmed the next required date.

harbor_p16_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_009.text: The storeman's employer required him to complete the paired-leaf training and gave the custody duty to another worker until the documented review was complete. He said this made him look untrustworthy in front of people he had worked beside for years. Wen replied that his tub had looked unclaimed in front of the same people. The room fell quiet. Song asked both to keep to the supported question. Yue wished the remark could have resolved something because it felt exact. It did not. Two people left with different humiliations, and the business still needed a person to receive tomorrow's papers.

harbor_p16_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_010.text: Outside, the messenger asked the storeman whether they might have lunch sometime without discussing leaves. The storeman said he did not know. The younger man's face closed. Yue almost stepped into their conversation, then saw the messenger ask again more plainly: he missed the jokes, and a lunch did not have to certify innocence. The storeman agreed to the following day. They walked in opposite directions. Friendship could attempt an ordinary repair after a finding, with no assurance that the old ease would return. Yue let them leave without borrowing the exchange for her own account of the harbor.

harbor_p16_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_011.text: Wen went straight to his workshop and checked T4's maker mark again. Peng Li's repaired door closed properly behind him. The tub stood where he had always intended it to stand, useful for trade and freighted with memories. Yue stopped by as a friend. Wen asked whether the hearing had made him sound unreasonable. Yue said wanting the specific failures named was reasonable. Wen asked about the rest. The visitor answered that fear did not have to become a winning claim before it counted as fear. Wen poured tea and said that answer would do for today.

harbor_p16_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_012.text: Shui Rong's crew contract comparison took place in a different office. All six crew had received the original undisputed voyage wages; the grounding interval remained its own question. The contractor's first offer covered twelve copper, two for each crew member, without release of the rest under the written acceptance terms. They accepted that portion through the competent route. The comparison then found another twelve due under the interval provision, giving four each for the supported disputed period. Twenty-four in total came from the contractor's account. No part came from the closed seven-hundred-sixty guarantee or the emergency reserve.

harbor_p16_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_013.text: The crew payment answer did not decide every cause of the barge grounding. Chart marks, pilot decisions and the stake gap still belonged to the transport review, with their own evidence and scope. Shui preferred having a wage answer now to waiting until every responsibility question became one vast case. Luo Tai agreed, though he worried future hiring would still judge them by gossip. The office preserved the acceptance terms and current referral. He Ming accompanied Shui home privately. They bought no celebratory feast; the money had ordinary obligations waiting. They allowed themselves one hot bowl and a quieter conversation.

harbor_p16_014.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p16_014.text: You have been living with this amount as if it were already gone. Now it is paid, and it may disappear into rent before you have time to feel rich. That does not make the answer small. You can send the share you planned and keep something for yourself if you choose. I am not offering to divide it for you. My brother has recently taught me how unpleasant that sounds even when I call it help. I can sit here while you decide which ordinary expense matters first. The soup will remain our only joint project.

harbor_p16_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_015.text: Shui laughed and said He Ming's brother should give lessons to the whole quay. Then she admitted she wanted a pair of gloves that fit instead of another remittance carrying every spare coin. Her parents needed support; her own hands also did work. She chose the amount privately and visited the seller after supper. The gloves were plain, bought with her own wage. She wore them on the walk back even though the evening was not cold enough to require them. He Ming said nothing about thrift. The new cloth looked like permission that Shui had finally given herself.

harbor_p16_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_016.text: Sui prepared the public storm explanation for a meeting at the restored shelter room. The port's full accountability review remained unfinished, but people needed the confirmed rescue sequence and current access status. Tired of rumors about the skiff, she wrote a heading that said the unsafe return had caused the emergency transfer. The sentence was true about the immediate need for rescue. Beneath it, however, the old clearance map and obstructing cart appeared only in a small later note. Han read the draft during the assigned public-status comparison and saw how the arrangement could imply the workers explained every failure.

harbor_p16_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_017.text: Han brought the draft to Sui before publication. The captain looked at the note, then said the workers did return against the closure instruction. Han agreed and asked why the conflicting waiting map did not receive equal visibility in the sequence. Sui said the rescue had succeeded despite the cart. Han asked whether despite was the whole public duty. The captain's face hardened. Yue sat nearby with the contact sources she had brought and felt the room change. A friendship could make a correction easier to hear, or make its speaker seem more disloyal than a stranger would.

harbor_p16_018.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p16_018.text: I do not want a public account that hides their return. I also do not want my notice buried because I am the person explaining it. Show me the version you think preserves both. I am angry at the question, which is a useful sign that I should stop defending the draft for a moment. Give me the sources in their order, including the old waiting mark. The independent reviewer will decide responsibility. My job here is to tell people what we have confirmed and what remains under review, without arranging the page to protect my face.

harbor_p16_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_019.text: Han rewrote the heading as a confirmed rescue sequence and put the clearance count, unreported return, obsolete cart mark and bank transfers in order. Each had its source. The explanation identified the pending port review rather than implying the public meeting had reached its findings. Sui signed the version and requested that her first draft be kept with the working record, so the change could be understood. Yue checked the contact portion and named what she had seen. The work took longer than expected. Sui bought everyone tea from her own purse afterward and did not ask to be thanked.

harbor_p16_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_020.text: At the public meeting, Ke Chun listened from a chair that matched her care restriction. Tong sat near the door. The captain explained the sequence in words before referring to the displayed page. One man asked why the port should spend rescue money on people who ignored instructions. Sui answered that the duty was to bring people ashore safely when a safe rescue was available. Conduct and costs could be reviewed through their own process. The answer drew muttering. Yue watched Ke keep her hands flat on her knees, as if any motion might become somebody else's evidence of ingratitude.

harbor_p16_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_021.text: Another attendee asked why the old cart mark remained in use. Sui said that exact question was in the independent port review, with her notice and the crew maps supplied. She described the interim correction already made and its receiving person. The man said captains always hid behind reviews. Her cheek's cut tightened when she smiled without pleasure. She said the current sources could be read under the office's stated access arrangements, and the final finding would identify responsibility. The meeting could ask a question sharply without turning its anger into proof. It could also make the room very hot.

harbor_p16_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_022.text: Bo stood to say the cart's owner had moved it when told. Han pointed to the already included source and thanked him for the confirmed observation. Bo sat down frustrated that a public room had no place for the dramatic defense he had prepared. Deren leaned over and whispered that competent silence had returned to collect its fee. The young rigger nearly laughed during somebody else's complaint and covered it badly. Yue saw Sui's eyes move toward them, then away. The captain allowed the small interruption to pass. Even a tense meeting could contain people with ordinary, badly timed amusement.

harbor_p16_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_023.text: When the meeting ended, Tong approached Ke and asked whether the room had heard they both returned. She said it had. He wanted to know whether she still blamed him for the jacket. She answered that she blamed herself for the tools and him for his choice, which was less comforting than he hoped. Then she showed him her needle's wrapper. He said it looked too small. She said beginnings did. They walked toward the work board. The public sequence had not repaired their shame, but it left less room for one person to carry all of it.

harbor_p16_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_024.text: Sui stayed to stack chairs after the keeper said her help was welcome. Han remained too, and the captain apologized for making the first correction difficult. The clerk accepted and admitted she had almost softened the question because she feared losing their ease. Sui said she would dislike that more, once she stopped being angry. They carried a bench together with ordinary hands from the safe lifting positions. Yue swept the floor with the keeper's broom, returning it afterward. Nobody made the cleanup symbolic aloud. It was a room that needed putting back before the next scheduled gathering.

harbor_p16_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_025.text: That night Sui wrote her son about the meeting. She did not send private claimant details, only the general fact that she had needed help correcting her own public draft. She asked whether the oven workshop had ever made a mistake look like a customer's fault by arranging the explanation too neatly. The letter was not a confession sent to a judge. It was a mother's honest question to a man whose work she often treated as simpler than hers. She folded it before she could replace the question with advice about the workshop's doors.

harbor_p16_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_026.text: Han found the captain's first draft harder to forget than Sui did. At home she looked at her own painted curve and saw how readily a pleasing line became a shape one wanted to protect. Duan would have mocked the comparison as another attempt to make painting serve office lessons. Han laughed alone and picked up the brush anyway. She painted an ordinary shell from memory, badly enough that it resembled a bent spoon. Yue arrived for their planned tea and said it was excellent cutlery. The clerk threatened to charge her rent for the notebook shelf after all.

harbor_p16_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_027.text: The joke ended in a quiet discussion about the coming cold. Han intended to remain at the wage office for the next ordinary term. Yue's fourteen-week appointment still had its stated end. The shelf could hold a notebook while she visited, but no furniture could negotiate the dates for them. Han asked whether Yue wanted to stay beyond the term. Yue said wanting and deciding were different at the moment. She had work ahead on the road, and she had friends here. The clerk accepted the unfinished answer without making it a secret promise. Then she poured the last tea.

harbor_p16_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_028.text: Fen accepted the account shop's paid trial beginning after the binder's agreed notice. She spoke to the binder herself and received the copying dates and wage settlement terms. Luo came only after she invited him to help read one section. He wanted to ask the aunt whether Fen would be safe, but asked the actual closing hour and return route instead. The aunt answered. On the walk home he said he would miss the binder's supper rhythm. Fen took his arm carefully on the uninjured side. She said they could make another rhythm without pretending the old one meant nothing.

harbor_p16_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_029.text: Aning gave Fen a blank page she owned, not a shop record. At the top she drew a terrible turnip bird like Wu's children had made. Fen said she might use it as her first account seal. Aning told her the aunt would faint. They laughed and began practice under the shop's lesson arrangement. The page remained personal learning material; actual customer records stayed with their keeper. Yue stopped outside long enough to see their heads bent over different columns. Two young women were making a future that could not be described only by whom they had found or left.

harbor_p16_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_030.text: At the partnership room, An's smaller private job completed under its own checked receipts and three agreed wage shares. The partners closed that notebook entry without borrowing from the earlier forty-eight contract, which was already settled. Wu did not work on this batch and owed no attendance. She came after the canteen with a portion of soup He Ming had ordered and paid for, then sat beneath the ugly gull. Zhou proposed a meeting about prices before the next offer. An asked whether the gull had a vote. He Ming said it had already abstained by looking in two directions.

harbor_p16_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_031.text: The public transfer summary reached the tea stall, where somebody immediately shortened it into a tale of four villains stealing one tub. Wen heard the version and corrected the number before correcting the accusation. All six containers had been held under the loan; one improper transfer was the supported event, and intentional theft had not been established. The storyteller accused him of defending men he had blamed. Wen said he was defending his own account from becoming entertainment. Miao, seated nearby, looked at his bowl and let him finish. He did not try to make his accuracy sound like forgiveness.

harbor_p16_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_032.text: Afterward Wen told Yue he disliked having to protect the finding from people who claimed to support him. Yue said a person could believe the wrong version for generous reasons and still need correcting. Wen grumbled that generosity ought to come with better ears. He returned to his workshop, where T4 needed an ordinary cleaning before the next permitted use. The tub's practical life would continue long after the hearing became a story people told inaccurately. Wen had no wish to spend that whole life repeating the same afternoon. He posted the precise summary and went back to work.

harbor_p16_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_033.text: Song An's office set the compliance check dates in the final notice and named the receiving clerks. Merchant dispatch terms, store leaf custody and carrier exception practice belonged to distinct duties. The public copy used the permitted names and acts without displaying private household addresses. Yue compared the posted route with the actual receiving room during her second scheduled half-day. One clerk had changed posts; the named substitute confirmed coverage in writing. The final paper would be less satisfying if the next person found an empty desk. Its answer needed somewhere ordinary to go after Yue stopped visiting.

harbor_p16_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_034.text: Rao Tong's employment review reached a supported result during the same week. The witness confirmed the relevant words about stopping pay after the strap report, and the employer's shift sheet showed six copper withheld for completed work. The competent reviewer directed that six to be paid from the employer's own account and required the report route to remain available under the applicable employment terms. The broader claim that every later unfavorable roster change was retaliation lacked the current support needed for that finding. Rao received the six and the separate answer together, pleased by one and frustrated by the other.

harbor_p16_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_035.text: He asked Han whether taking the money meant agreeing about the roster. The written terms preserved his stated further review route; receiving the undisputed wage did not erase it. She helped him locate the actual deadline and kept the detailed decision in proper custody. Yue encountered Rao outside afterward. He said he had imagined justice would feel more complete. She asked what the six would do tonight. Rent, he answered, then laughed without pleasure. The payment mattered exactly enough to keep a room. His remaining worry mattered too. They walked to the stall, where neither truth canceled the other.

harbor_p16_036.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p16_036.text: I used to think an answer with several parts looked weak beside a simple verdict. Now I think of Rao keeping his room while deciding what to do about the roster. The six had to be paid. The other question had to be described honestly. If we tied them together, somebody would have waited for money already supported while we chased a broader conclusion. He can be dissatisfied with the result and still use it. We should not ask gratitude as the price of explaining the next step. I would like that written above my desk, mainly for me.

harbor_p16_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_037.text: Qin said a sign above a desk became invisible after a month. Han asked whether he offered a better method. He suggested she keep a friend who would point at the sign while she ignored it. Yue raised her hand from the other side of the tea table. The three laughed. Qin's custodian arrived to collect him for their ordinary handover, and he left without adding another lesson. Han admitted she liked his shorter visits better now that he had something beyond wage custody to discuss. The garden was not thriving, but it had given him another subject.

harbor_p16_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_038.text: At home Qin found one replanted bean seedling had emerged after all. He had planted it cautiously after the soil recovered, not in defiance of the earlier lesson. He spent a ridiculous interval examining its two small leaves. His late wife's old cup stood beside him on the garden bench. He said aloud that the plant seemed willing, then felt embarrassed by talking to an absent woman and an unresponsive bean. Nobody heard. The ordinary private moment did not make grief finished. It let him enjoy a small living thing without asking what duty entitled him to the pleasure.

harbor_p16_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_039.text: Dai Min received payment for the net repair completed around the lamp she had bought. She used part to obtain sound thread for the next job and part for a private visit to her sister inland. The death and wage records concerning her husband stayed at their keepers; she carried the personal comb that had been returned to her. She told He Ming she wanted the visit because her sister knew stories from before the harbor. The trip was not a search for a missing ending. She had a room to return to and a reason to leave it briefly.

harbor_p16_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_040.text: He Ming offered to water Dai's small plant during the trip, then asked the actual interval before promising. Dai said three days. The plant had suffered more from previous enthusiastic watering than from drought. He Ming agreed to the specific amount with comic solemnity. Wu overheard and said this partnership should charge the plant a custody fee. Dai threatened to appoint the duck as independent reviewer. The three women laughed in the work room, where Han's ugly gull witnessed the arrangement. A friendship could manage a living obligation without pretending it resembled every wage and cargo case they had known.

harbor_p16_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_041.text: Dai departed on the licensed cart after the road report confirmed the route. She paid from her income and carried only the luggage she chose. Yue watched the cart leave from beyond the loading boundary and envied the clarity of a three-day journey with a named return. Her own next road stretched into a kiln town she did not yet know. No harbor friend could negotiate its work for her. She had done that before in other places, yet the uncertainty felt different. She was not afraid only of failing there. She was afraid of being happy here and leaving.

harbor_p16_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_042.text: The coast's days were shortening. At the partnership room working hours now needed an earlier finish unless the next quote covered proper evening light and safe attendance. Zhou wanted to add a lamp. An wanted to take the next smaller batch during daylight instead. He Ming checked buyer timing before choosing between them. There was no urgent need to buy a new object merely because the idea sounded like progress. Wu's canteen hours still limited her availability. The partners made one daytime proposal and waited for the answer, which left them an unpaid afternoon free for their own lives.

harbor_p16_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_043.text: He Ming used that afternoon to visit the storage warehouse with An. Their rented work room had enough space for current jobs but little dry stock room if trade grew. The warehouse keeper offered a shelf lease for sound wrapping, with access hours and no promise that every disaster would leave stock intact. An examined the roof and the stove pipe in the keeper's break corner. A recent repair patch stood near the flue. The keeper showed the contractor's clearance and said a reported loose edge had a follow-up appointment. He Ming wanted that date written before considering a lease.

harbor_p16_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_044.text: The follow-up lay in the next work week. The partners deferred the shelf agreement until the inspection rather than move materials today. Their stock remained in the existing room. The keeper looked disappointed but accepted the reason and recorded it. Yue heard the account at supper through He Ming, identifying it as her visit rather than a site Yue had inspected. The warehouse itself continued its ordinary approved operation under the existing clearance, with the reported edge waiting for comparison. A paper could show why people believed a place usable. It could not itself examine the patch when weather shifted.

harbor_p16_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_045.text: Yan's rigging crew had an ordinary delivery task at that warehouse later in the week. He saw the keeper's reported-edge notice and asked the site supervisor whether the break corner remained in use. The supervisor pointed to the current clearance and the arranged visit. Yan did not invent a technical finding outside his competence. He forwarded his observed concern to the building maintenance contact and kept the loading task away from the break corner's obstruction. Later the source would matter. At that moment it was simply a man doing his own job while asking somebody else to check theirs.

harbor_p16_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_046.text: Bo wanted to fetch the repair shed boy's kite for a fine afternoon flight. The boy's parent approved the ordinary visit to the open inland yard, well away from quay work and cargo. Fen came after the binder's final copying task, bringing the repaired tail. Aning held the spool while the boy ran. The fish rose lopsidedly, dipped and caught enough wind to make everybody shout at once. Yue stood beside Han watching private names trail beneath it. They were too small to read from the ground. The boy no longer seemed troubled by that. He knew who was aboard.

harbor_p16_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_047.text: The line tangled in a low bush rather than a warehouse roof. Bo retrieved the paper from the permitted safe side after stopping the child's running, with no climbing and no qi intervention. The boy accused the bush of piracy. Fen said it had only claimed temporary storage. The tail had lost one scrap, which they found beneath a leaf. They put the kite away before dusk and went to the stall for tea. Its brief flight had no consequences for public rights or harbor reform. It mattered because they had wanted a clear afternoon together and finally received one.

harbor_p16_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_048.text: Luo joined them late after sorting paper at the binder. His trial of increased hand use remained within the plan, and he had completed a light basket task without the sharp pain he feared. He told Fen, then immediately warned that recovery still had limits. She said she knew and wanted to hear the good part twice. He repeated it. The young repair shed boy asked whether his fingers would grow back. Luo answered honestly and then showed what the motion could do with the kite spool. The boy accepted the demonstration without needing a perfect body to admire it.

harbor_p16_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_049.text: Fen's last binder wage arrived on the agreed settlement date. She thanked the owner for the paid copying and sorted her personal learning pages from the shop's records before leaving. The borrowed board and task pencils went back to the keeper. She bought one ordinary pencil for her own arithmetic practice with her wage, an acquisition small enough to explain and large enough to make her happy. At home Luo asked whether she wanted him to sharpen it. She said yes. He used the safe ordinary tool with care and gave it back as if handing her a key.

harbor_p16_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_050.text: Aning's aunt showed Fen the trial stool and named the employee who would teach the first column. Customer files remained within the shop's custody. Fen's early mistakes would be checked before actual dispatch or payment decisions used her work. The arrangement gave her room to learn without calling it authority she had not earned. She liked the practical stool, the view of the lane and the aunt's refusal to pretend the work would always be interesting. Aning whispered that the dull parts were excellent for discovering whether she truly liked numbers. Fen said she liked wages, which was a start.

harbor_p16_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_051.text: He Jun's reply about the quilt thanked He Ming for her contribution and enclosed their mother's message. The older woman had selected a plain warm quilt and wanted neither child to turn it into proof of family rank. She was proud of He Ming's work and Jun's repair job in different ways. He Ming read the sentence twice, hoping to find a preference and ashamed of the hope. Zhou watched her face and asked whether the blanket had won another argument. He Ming said her mother remained an unfairly skilled opponent, then kept the letter safely in her own room.

harbor_p16_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_052.text: Miao's reduced voyage schedule left him free on an afternoon when he would previously have inspected a loading list. He visited the ordinary tool seller and asked about stock, rent and failed purchases. The seller answered some questions and refused to disclose his entire account. Miao accepted the limit. He bought nothing and made no claim to have begun a new trade. His fantasy shop became less magnificent and more possible after the conversation. He told Yue later that learning costs had spoiled the dream's cheapest pleasure. She said it might improve the dream's chances of surviving a real morning.

harbor_p16_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_053.text: The agency employer asked Miao to handle one routine waiting-pay comparison under the revised terms. He did, using the gate source and the carrier's own account to settle the supported interval from the merchant's money. The task was less profitable than the imagined bonus and less likely to reward silence. He sent the corrected dispatch with both leaves attached through the receipt routine. Nobody applauded. The work went where it needed to go. Afterward he bought his supper and felt briefly resentful that improvement looked so much like an ordinary day. Then he recognized that ordinary days were the point.

harbor_p16_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_054.text: Sui left for the approved inland visit at the end of the week after the replacement captain accepted the ordinary port handover. Her personal fare came from her own purse. The harbor's independent review continued with its named officers while she was away; no claimant needed to wait for her private return to submit a source. She carried a small loaf she had made successfully and a letter with questions for her son. Yue saw her at the cart stand and asked whether the loaf had passed inspection. Sui said the inspector had been dismissed for eating too much evidence.

harbor_p16_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_055.text: Without the captain's familiar figure, the quay looked briefly less settled to Yue. Then the replacement captain called a lane closure for a scheduled load, and the crew responded in the known order. The port continued through roles rather than affection for one face. Han joined Yue at the doorway and said Sui would be angry if they used her holiday to discover she was mortal. Yue laughed. The clerk added that being missed was allowed. They watched the cleared cart leave, then returned to a contact task whose receiving hour would end whether or not the captain was there.

harbor_p16_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_056.text: Yue's two completed half-days earned another four copper. Six paid the week's bed and meals, bringing the new term to seventy-four spent and one hundred twenty-six unspent after twelve paid half-days. No new field fare or interpretation fee was charged from that appointment this week. The separate reserve remained one hundred thirty spent, one hundred ten unspent, with four unused stones. The public findings credited existing payments and used the contractor's and employer's accounts for the new crew and withheld-wage amounts. Yue kept those sources separate in her own brief note, then put the pen down before supper.

harbor_p16_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p16_057.text: The eighteenth week's last evening brought a smell of wood smoke across the lane. It came from a cooking fire whose owner had the permitted stove and clear flue; nobody raised an alarm simply because the memory of danger was fresh. Han opened her window to listen to the canteen's closing voices. Yue took her notebook from the borrowed shelf space and tucked it in her pack. They had planned another walk tomorrow. The harbor's cases were becoming answers, its rooms becoming familiar and its people becoming harder to leave. None of them knew which ordinary room would change next.
